questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a variable in Python?
options: A labeled storage box in memory that holds a value for later use
A command that immediately shuts down the computer
A physical cable connecting your monitor to the CPU
A special key on your keyboard that only types numbers
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! A variable is a named reference in memory where you store a value to reuse later in your program.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. A variable is a labeled storage box in computer memory that holds data.

questions.question: Which line of Python code correctly creates a variable named 'score' with the value 100?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! The variable name always goes on the left side of the single '=' assignment operator, and the value goes on the right.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Remember the rule: the box name always goes on the LEFT side of '=', value on the RIGHT.

questions.question: If you write `age = 25`, what will `print(age)` display vs `print("age")`?
options: print(age) displays 25, while print("age") displays the word age
Both lines display the word age
It causes an error because quotes are never allowed
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! print(age) without quotes opens the variable box and shows 25, while print("age") in quotes treats it as plain text.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Without quotes, Python evaluates the variable name. With quotes, it prints the literal text.

questions.question: What happens if you try to `print(total)` before writing `total = 50`?
options: Python crashes with a NameError because the box total has not been created yet
Python automatically guesses the value is 0
Python prints nothing and moves on silently
Python waits for you to type the value on the keyboard
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Python executes top-to-bottom. You cannot open a variable box before you create it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Python executes in order from top to bottom. Trying to use an uncreated variable raises a NameError.
